original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a satellite system for FRMCS which is operating in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial counterpart (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), with the purpose to exclusively service the coverage gaps of the terrestrial network while avoiding interference. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

original.description: Plasma Observatory aims to study the fundamental processes responsible for plasma energisation and energy transport around shocks and near-Earth space. The mission is comprised of 7 identical sister spinning spacecraft, launched by Ariane 64 and operated on a high-elliptic orbit.The Phase B1 System Study has the following objectives:- Complete outstanding trade-offs- Consolidate requirements and interfaces- Issue of Requests for Information (RFIs) for platform subsystems and/or equipment-  Refine the development risk assessment (major risks and mitigation)- Consolidate the development and verification plan, including baseline master schedule- Refine the estimate of the industrial costs- Conduct a dialogue phase with ESA to consolidate implementation requirements (in preparation of Phase B2/C/D/E1 Invitation to Tender)- Support the Mission Adoption Review (MAR)

original.description: This activity will evaluate the technical and commercial feasibility of developing a standardised and interoperable set of Flat Panel User Terminal (UT) building blocks and internal interfaces, able to be reused in end user equipment designed for deployment across a broad range of market sectors and network types.The objective is to support the creation of a scalable, industrialised and costcompetitive ecosystem for flat panel user terminals in the ESA Member States by enabling economies of scale through open architectures and harmonised specifications.The activity will also identify standardised FPA terminal profiles (classes'), defining their RFperformance characteristics and associated validation and certification methodologies, to facilitate objective performance assessment and enable fair and interoperable competition among vendors.

original.description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of resilient PNT payload technologies based on digital and AI-enabled architectures. The study will investigate reconfigurable, software-defined payloads capable of characterizing and adapting to dynamic, congested or impaired RF environments.The activity will address the full signal chain, from generation to transmission, including onboard processing and AI-based techniques. A digital twin environment is also foreseen to be developed to support validation andperformance assessment.The objective is to mature concept and associated key payload technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible, flight-representative architecture for next-generation PNT systems.

original.description: The objective(s) of this activity are the following:a) Design and implement an end-to-end Space Segment testbed that can constitute a security reference architecture, including a number of cyber security building blocks.b) Perform a security assessment and verification of the implemented security measures using the selected cyber security building blocks.c) Identify potential security enhancements, that can constitute candidates for further technical developments into products.The targeted current Technology ReadinessLevel (TRL) of this activity is 4 [RD1].WORK TO BE PERFORMED1 Work LogicThe work will be organised in two phases and the following tasks:Phase 1: Definition of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 1: State-of-the-art survey of mission scenarios, security threats, relevant legislations and regulations and security technologiesoTask 2: Consolidationof Space Segment modular security reference architecture, including identification of required cyber security building blocks andspecification of system Space Segment security requirements.oTask 3: Specification of Space Segment testbed requirements (including incorporated cyber security building blocks), design and implementation and test planningPhase 2: Development, implementation and testing of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 4: Development of the Space Segment testbedoTask 5: Space Segment Testbed Testing, Security Assessment and Vulnerability MitigationoTask 6: Lessons learnt and proposed roadmap for further (other than [RD16] building blocks development (including high level specifications)Note that phase 2 will be authorised to implement the agreed building blocks, subject to a successful Phase 1 and acceptance of a proposal for the conversion of the Phase 2 price from ceilingprice to Firm Fixed Price.
